quick_notes.title: Industrial Clusters
quick_notes.detail: 1. Chennai (Automobiles - Detroit of Asia). 2. Tiruppur (Knitwear/Textiles - Manchester of South). 3. Sivakasi (Fireworks/Matchboxes - Little Japan). 4. Namakkal (Egg/Poultry & Truck body building). 5. Karur (Coach building).
quick_notes.explanation: An industrial cluster is a specific area or region where many factories and businesses that make the same type of product are located close together. In Tamil Nadu, there are several famous industrial clusters. Chennai is known for making automobiles, or cars and vehicles, and is sometimes called the Detroit of Asia, referring to the famous car-making city in the United States. Tiruppur is a cluster for knitwear and textiles, meaning it produces clothing like T-shirts and fabric, and is called the Manchester of South, after a famous textile city in England. Sivakasi is a cluster for fireworks, like Diwali sparklers, and matchboxes, and is nicknamed Little Japan because Japan is known for its small-scale manufacturing. Namakkal is a cluster for eggs and poultry, meaning chicken farming, as well as for building the bodies of trucks. Karur is a cluster for building the bodies of buses, which is called coach building.

quick_notes.title: Special Economic Zones (SEZ)
quick_notes.detail: TN has a high number of operational SEZs. Nanguneri (Multi-product), Ennore (Thermal power), Perambalur (Specialty chemicals).
quick_notes.explanation: Special Economic Zones (SEZs) are specific geographic areas within a country where business and trade laws are different from the rest of the country to encourage economic activity. The main goal of an SEZ is to attract foreign investment, boost exports, and create jobs by offering tax breaks, simpler regulations, and better infrastructure. Tamil Nadu has a large number of operational SEZs, meaning zones that are already running and producing goods or services. Examples include the Nanguneri SEZ, which is a multi-product zone handling various types of goods; the Ennore SEZ, which is dedicated to thermal power generation; and the Perambalur SEZ, which focuses on specialty chemicals. These zones are governed by the Special Economic Zones Act of 2005, which provides the legal framework for their setup and operation.

quick_notes.title: GI Tags of TN
quick_notes.detail: Highest in India. Famous : Kanchipuram Silk, Srivilliputhur Palkova, Dindigul Locks, Kovilpatti Kadalai Mittai, Madurai Malli.
quick_notes.explanation: Geographical Indication or GI tag is a special label given to products that come from a specific place and have unique qualities because of that location. Tamil Nadu, abbreviated as TN, has the highest number of GI tags among all Indian states. Some famous GI-tagged products from Tamil Nadu include Kanchipuram Silk, which is a handwoven silk saree made in Kanchipuram; Srivilliputhur Palkova, a sweet milk-based confection from Srivilliputhur; Dindigul Locks, strong iron locks made in Dindigul; Kovilpatti Kadalai Mittai, a peanut brittle sweet from Kovilpatti; and Madurai Malli, which is a fragrant jasmine flower grown in Madurai.

quick_notes.title: Mineral Resources
quick_notes.explanation: TITLE: Mineral Resources This lesson introduces four important minerals found in the Indian state of Tamil Nadu. First, lignite is a type of brown coal that is softer and lower in energy than black coal, and it is mined in large amounts at Neyveli. Second, magnesite is a mineral used to make heat-resistant bricks and other products, and it is found in the Salem district. Third, garnet and ilmenite are heavy minerals that are extracted from the black sand along the coast, particularly for use in abrasives and titanium production (ilmenite is the main source of titanium metal). Fourth, limestone is a common rock used mainly to make cement and in construction, and a major deposit is located in the Ariyalur region.

quick_notes.title: Ports & Logistics
quick_notes.detail: 3 Major Ports: Ennore (Kamarajar), Chennai, Tuticorin (V.O.C). Development of Industrial Corridors (CBIC, VCIC).
quick_notes.explanation: Ports are places where ships load and unload goods, and logistics is the system of moving those goods by road, rail, or sea. In Tamil Nadu, there are three major ports: Ennore Port, which is officially called Kamarajar Port; Chennai Port; and Tuticorin Port, which is officially called V.O.C. Port (named after V.O. Chidambaram Pillai). The government is also developing two Industrial Corridors, which are special zones with factories and transport links to boost trade: the Chennai Bengaluru Industrial Corridor (CBIC) and the Visakhapatnam Chennai Industrial Corridor (VCIC). These corridors connect the ports to inland cities so that goods can travel faster and cheaper.
